messages.subject: filter issue with Deducer
parts:
Hi all,

Not sure if this is a native R 13.1 issue or Deducer issue.

I need to import (i.e. create new data set by pasting) and filter it to
create a new subset/.

Issue 1. The time does not correctly format. It is listed as a
character string and when I use variable view in the Data Viewer time is
listed as Character. That date was also initially but accepted as
character and when changed to date format YYYYMMDD all is fine. Time
does not and when I change for character (e.g. 20:02) to a time value
using other HH:MM the data values disappear from the data set.

It is saved an *robj file so I can restore it with original values.

If I ignore the time and just treat it as a character and try to do a
subset Data>subset from the console and chose the field (Character) I
need to use as the filter, I have a message "Invalid subset, please
enter a logical expression."

A logical expression was selected: e.g. Species == Ptequa, where by the
"Species" field is a character string.

Short of using Excel and filtering the data set prior to adding to
Deducer/R I would really get this to work in Deducer.

It seemed to work a few versions back w/o any issues.

An update to # 13.1 or recent Deducer issue or some basic syntax I am
missing?

Tnx,

Bruce


--
Bruce W. Miller, Ph.D.

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: filter issue with Deducer
parts:
Hi Bruce,

Just getting back from vacation...

Time is not clock time, but rather date-time. so you can't represent
something like 5:30, but you could represent 01-11-2011 5:30.

Next, you need quotes around your species name in your subset expression:

Species == "Ptequa"

cheers,
Ian
